智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), enhancing LLM evaluation by addressing judgment uncertainty in rubric-based assessments to improve reinforcement learning outcomes.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Rubric-based evaluation is widely used to assess large language model (LLM) outputs by decomposing quality into multiple criteria and assigning each a binary judgment from an LLM verifier. However, judgment certainty varies substantially across criteria. Existing methods uniformly aggregate these judgments into a final score, implicitly treating every criterion as equally certain and overlooking this heterogeneity. As a result, uncertain judgments remain incorporated into reward estimation without distinction, potentially yielding misleading training signals for downstream reinforcement learning (RL). To address this limitation, we propose Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), a training-free framework that quantifies criterion-level judgment uncertainty via conformal calibration. Specifically, URW elicits a soft uncertainty signal from a fixed pool of paraphrased judgment templates and converts it into a per-criterion weight using split-conformal $p$-values with provable coverage guarantees. Extensive experiments demonstrate that URW consistently improves pairwise preference accuracy and delivers stronger downstream RL alignment.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: ReasonUni: Reasoning-Augmented Reconstruction Advances Unified Multimodal Models
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Feize Wu, Zhiyuan Yan, Yuhuan Hong, Yuwei Niu, Zongjian Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: ReasonUni enhances unified multimodal models by integrating reasoning into reconstructive post-training, improving image-to-text understanding and text-to-image generation through a novel reinforcement learning approach.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. We propose ReasonUni, a reasoning-augmented reconstructive post-training framework that extends this coupling beyond perception. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. To jointly optimize both modules, we introduce TreeGRPO, a tree-structured reinforcement learning method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path, then aggregates visual rewards to update both modules under a unified objective. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains in both understanding and generation, showing that reasoning-augmented reconstruction yields genuine mutual gains for UMMs.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Ningxin Pan, Hanyu Li, Yeqing Shen, Ning Ding, Yehui Tang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces RealtimeBench for evaluating LLM agents in dynamic environments and proposes TORSI to enhance their performance through structured learning across timescales.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. Two rounds raise Jev's average test score from 13.51 to 24.19 on a 0--100 progress scale, improving all six game types. The instructions also improve average scores for three other models without retuning. These findings point toward real-time intelligence: enabling powerful LLM agents to remain effective in a continuously changing world by organizing deliberation, learning, and action across timescales.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: RAP-WAM: Learning World-Action Models through Predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yuanpeng He, Ceyao Zhang, Fangjing Li, Kefei Zhu, Lijian Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: RAP-WAM enhances policy learning in robotics by integrating predictive rehearsal and action perturbations, achieving significant performance improvements across various tasks without requiring separate scoring networks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Recent world action models draw on video generation priors to jointly predict future observations and robot actions. Adapting these priors to control requires determining how future predictions should guide policy learning. RAP-WAM combines predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations (RAP) with future-supervised queries and Coupled Action Projection for policy learning. Predictive rehearsal trains on model-generated inputs while retaining recorded targets, and accumulates recurring errors into a spatial prior. We perturb actions and measure changes in video predictions. Action-response-based spatiotemporal credit assignment combines these responses, prediction error, and the rehearsal prior to allocate visual supervision; spatially aggregating the responses determines supervision intensity across future action steps. No separate scoring network or deployment-time probe is required. The base learns from a video-pretrained backbone without intermediate pretraining on external embodied data. We evaluate the fixed base and its agent-refined, task-conditioned system. On 42 RoboDojo tasks, their average success rates are 12.85% and 15.62%, with Scores of 17.86 and 20.59. Across 15 real-robot tasks, the complete system achieves 89.00% task-macro-average success, exceeding the strongest of five baselines by 37.67 percentage points. Across 315 fixed-output simulation windows, 45.21% of response-top20 positions fall outside error-top20, revealing information beyond prediction error. Videos and further details are available on the project website: https://rapwam.github.io/.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Revisiting Embodied Chain-of-Thought for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Nan Sun, Yuan Zhang, Yongkun Yang, Wentao Zhao, Peiyan Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: This paper introduces ERVLA, a vision-language-action model that enhances robotic manipulation through effective embodied chain-of-thought integration, achieving state-of-the-art performance in diverse tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Embodied chain-of-thought (CoT) aims to bridge linguistic reasoning with robotic control, yet its effective form and integration remain underexplored. In this paper, we revisit embodied CoT for robotic control at an unprecedented scale. We curate the largest embodied CoT corpus to date, comprising 978,743 trajectories, 226.3M samples, and 2592.5 hours of data. Through extensive experiments, we show that effective CoT must ground high-level semantic understaning in concrete linguistic action guidance -- such as end-effector movement and image-space trajectories -- whereas high-level reasoning alone yields marginal gains. More importantly, we identify that explicit CoT does not scale reliably as an autoregressive action prefix, suffering from compounding errors during inference. To address these challenges, we propose ERVLA, a vision-language-action (VLA) model that effectively leverages linguistic reasoning in generalizable robot manipulation. ERVLA is trained using a CoT-dropout strategy, allowing the model to leverage rich reasoning traces during training while predicting actions directly without CoT during inference to bypass autoregressive instability. This approach enables reliable scaling with increasing pre-training data. ERVLA achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO-Plus with an 86.9\% success rate and reaches 53.2\% on VLABench, showcasing superior performance in out-of-distribution settings. Furthermore, ERVLA outperforms competitive state-of-the-art baselines in real-robot experiments, especially in handling semantic ambiguity and long-horizon tasks. Code, data, and model checkpoints are available on the project website: https://taoshuaiz.github.io/ERVLA/.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Adapting the Interface, Not the Model: Runtime Harness Adaptation for Deterministic LLM Agents
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Tianshi Xu, Huifeng Wen, Meng Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents Life-Harness, a runtime adaptation method for LLM agents that enhances performance by addressing interface mismatches without altering model weights.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: LLM agents are shaped not only by their language models, but also by the runtime harness that mediates observation, tool use, action execution, feedback interpretation, and trajectory control. While existing agent adaptation methods mainly update model parameters, many failures in deterministic, rule-governed domains stem from mismatches at the model--environment interface. We propose Life-Harness, a lifecycle-aware runtime harness that improves frozen LLM agents without changing model weights or evaluation environments. Life-Harness evolves from training trajectories by converting recurring interaction failures into reusable interventions across environment contracts, procedural skills, action realization, and trajectory regulation, and remains fixed for evaluation on unseen tasks. We evaluate Life-Harness across eight environments from AgentBench, $τ$-bench, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld using 18 open-weight backbones, and further test three frontier models on seven environments. With Qwen3-4B-Instruct, Life-Harness exceeds Meta-Harness and AHE by 28.7 and 7.5 percentage points in mean accuracy across the seven shared environments, respectively, while using 8.5\% and 68.4\% fewer optimization tokens. The evolved harnesses also benefit GPT 5.5, Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, yielding an average accuracy gain of 3.5 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/Tianshi-Xu/Life-Harness.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: PhyMix: Towards Physically Consistent Single-Image 3D Indoor Scene Generation with Implicit--Explicit Optimization
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Dongli Wu, Jingyu Hu, Ka-Hei Hui, Xiaobao Wei, Chengwen Luo
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: PhyMix enhances single-image 3D indoor scene generation by incorporating a Physics Evaluator and optimization strategies to ensure physical consistency while maintaining visual fidelity.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Existing methods for single-image 3D indoor scene generation often produce visually plausible results that violate real-world physical constraints, limiting their reliability in robotics, embodied AI, and virtual environment design. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Physics Evaluator that assesses four aspects (geometric priors, contact, stability, and deployability) through nine sub-constraints, establishing a benchmark for evaluating physical consistency. Our analysis reveals that even state-of-the-art methods produce scenes with substantial physical inconsistencies despite their visual plausibility. To address these limitations, we propose a framework that incorporates feedback from the Physics Evaluator into both training and inference to improve the physical plausibility of generated scenes. Specifically, PhyMix comprises two components: (i) implicit alignment via Scene-GRPO, a critic-free group-relative preference optimization strategy that uses physical evaluations to guide the generator toward physically plausible layouts, and (ii) explicit refinement via verifier-guided agentic repair, which translates evaluator diagnostics into executable scene-editing skills to correct residual violations at inference time. PhyMix unifies physical evaluation, preference-based alignment, and agentic inference-time correction to improve physical plausibility while retaining the observed scene content. Experiments show improvements in reconstruction quality and physical plausibility, while qualitative examples on stylized and real-world images illustrate the applicability of the framework beyond synthetic inputs.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Stabilizing the Modality Gap: Null-Space Projected Continual Learning for Vision-Language Models
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Tiantian Peng, Yuyang Liu, Shuo Yang, Qiuhe Hong, YongHong Tian
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents FPCD, a framework that mitigates modality gap drift in continual learning for vision-language models by combining Fast Null-space Projection and Contrastive Distillation, achieving superior performance on benchmark tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: The modality gap is intrinsic to multimodal alignment, where embeddings from different modalities remain partially separated in a shared representation space. In continual learning, CLIP-based vision-language models (VLMs) not only suffer catastrophic forgetting but also experience modality gap drift that disrupts the shared embedding geometry. Such drift degrades cross-modal alignment and generalization. We propose FPCD, an efficient framework combining Fast Null-space Projection (FNP) and Contrastive Distillation (CD). FNP accumulates compact Gram matrices of previous tasks' activations and projects gradients onto layer-adaptive approximate null spaces to reduce interference with learned representations. By replacing singular value decomposition with symmetric eigendecomposition, FNP accelerates projection-basis construction by a factor of 5-9. CD uses a small reference set to align the bidirectional image-to-text and text-to-image similarity distributions of the fine-tuned model with CLIP, thereby preserving pretrained cross-modal relations. On the 11-task MTIL benchmark, FPCD achieves 87.6% Last, 76.4% Average, and 65.2% Transfer. It also maintains more stable modality gaps and stronger zero-shot retrieval performance on COCO Captions and Flickr30k than competing methods. These results highlight the importance of controlling modality gap drift during continual adaptation of VLMs.

HMI Lab.title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
HMI Lab.authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
HMI Lab.summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for enhanced goal-directed generation across various domains.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

HMI Lab.title: Blame Errant Words, Not the Canvas: Defect-Aware Spatial Credit Assignment for Visual Text Generation
HMI Lab.authors_text: Sujie Hu, Huaisong Zhang, Pujing Yang, Qian Wang, Xiaomin Li
HMI Lab.summary: The paper presents TextDART and SCANNER, innovative models for defect-aware spatial credit assignment in visual text generation, enhancing accuracy and glyph quality through localized feedback.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. We identify two coupled limitations: recognition-based rewards often overlook visible glyph defects, while whole-image scalar feedback obscures the uneven quality of individual text regions. These limitations motivate our central principle: $\textit{Blame errant words, not the canvas}$, to effectively preserve local quality distinctions. First, we introduce $\mathbf{TextDART}$, a defect-aware region-targeted reward model that localizes individual text regions and independently evaluates their semantic correctness and glyph quality, providing fine-grained, region-precise feedback. Building on TextDART, we propose $\mathbf{SCANNER}$, which turns these regional judgments into spatially differentiated policy feedback. It normalizes rewards for each text target across sampled images and casts the resulting regional advantages onto the corresponding latent tokens. Extensive experiments on existing benchmarks and our newly established $\textbf{PolyText-Bench}$ demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in text accuracy and glyph fidelity. Project page: https://sujiehu.github.io/textdart-scanner

HMI Lab.title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
HMI Lab.authors_text: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiaye Lin, Ontai Tang, Jingtian Hao
HMI Lab.summary: MMSearch-OPD enhances long-horizon multimodal search agents through controllable data refinement, joint reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation, improving training and search capabilities.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

HMI Lab.title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos
HMI Lab.authors_text: Zhuoming Liu, Jinhong Lin, Lin Zhang, Yiwu Zhong, Yin Li
HMI Lab.summary: The MaLoW framework internalizes historical context as lightweight parameter updates in streaming vision-language models, enhancing performance while minimizing latency and generalizing to action tasks.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

HMI Lab.title: When Reasoning Is Not Enough: Proactive Inquiry for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
HMI Lab.authors_text: Wei Cai, Jian Zhao, Yuchen Yuan, Xuelong Li
HMI Lab.summary: The paper introduces SAFE-PRO, a proactive inquiry framework enhancing safety in multimodal large language models by addressing intent-level risks and optimizing safety through clarifying questions.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can act unsafely when individually benign images and texts are interpreted jointly. Beyond implicit reasoning risk, where reasoning drifts toward harm, we identify intent-level risk, where cross-modal ambiguity silently commits the model to a hazardous premise that path-level optimization alone cannot correct. We propose SAFE-PRO, which uses a Risk-Conditioned Uncertainty (RCU) signal, combining predictive entropy with a learned cross-modal risk score, to decide when to ask safety-grounded clarifying questions and where to apply path optimization, under a reward that prioritizes safety and penalizes over-refusal. We also build SSUI-Dialog, a multimodal multi-turn dataset with dual-intent supervision, and theoretically analyze gradient variance and unsafe-completion risk under RCU. Across seven benchmarks and two base MLLMs, SAFE-PRO consistently improves safety over SRPO, roughly halves its over-refusal, and surpasses GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet in average single-turn safety.

HMI Lab.title: What Should Robot Policies Learn to Predict? Rethinking Supervision Targets in Vision-Language-Action Learning
HMI Lab.authors_text: Haitao Shen, Hanyu Liu, Yihan Lin, Huiping Liu, Junbo Cui
HMI Lab.summary: This paper proposes a unified framework for vision-language-action learning that optimally allocates training samples between action prediction and auxiliary objectives, enhancing policy performance.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are typically trained with action prediction as the primary supervision signal, since robots ultimately execute actions. Auxiliary objectives such as latent-action (LA) and future-vision (FV) prediction are often added to improve policy learning, yet they compete with action prediction for the same training budget. We ask whether, under a fixed budget, allocating a substantial share of training samples to such objectives, rather than to further action prediction, can improve policy learning. We build a unified VLA framework that couples a two-stream multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) with a sample-level router, which assigns each training sample to either action prediction or an auxiliary objective and thus makes supervision allocation explicit. Within this framework, we instantiate three LA targets based on LAPA and its DINO-feature variants, and three FV targets based on DINOv3, V-JEPA 2, and Wan2.2 representations. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, and four real-robot tasks, suitable LA and FV supervision outperforms action-only training under the same budget, even when action prediction receives no more than half of the training samples. FV generally outperforms LA, although the strongest LA target remains competitive on CALVIN. Diagnostic analyses suggest that DINO-based LA targets emphasize relative motion, whereas FV targets emphasize absolute position and task identity. We therefore argue that what robot policies learn to predict, and how training is allocated among these targets, should be treated as explicit design choices rather than defaulting to action-dominant training.

HMI Lab.title: Uni-PNP: Unified Prehensile and Non-prehensile Policy Learning for Generalizable Object Pose Reaching
HMI Lab.authors_text: Wenxuan Zhu, Yuze Wang, Jiangran Lyu, Jiayi Chen, Yixin Zheng
HMI Lab.summary: Uni-PNP introduces a unified policy for simultaneous prehensile and non-prehensile object manipulation, achieving superior performance in diverse scenarios compared to existing methods.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Object manipulation often requires combining non-prehensile actions with grasping. However, existing approaches typically develop these capabilities separately and integrate them by sequencing distinct primitives through prescribed intermediate objectives, limiting the coordination of contact motions and grasping. Their integration also remains sensitive to object and gripper geometry and depends on particular environmental supports, complicating real-world deployment. We present Uni-PNP, a unified policy that jointly learns prehensile and non-prehensile manipulation for object pose reaching across diverse objects and grippers. To achieve this, we first pretrain a geometry encoder to predict contact-induced object motion using a contact-dynamics dataset constructed from simulated interactions between diverse objects and grippers. We then train the policy in a two-stage reinforcement learning curriculum from graspable objects to ungraspable peers, encouraging the discovery of non-prehensile interactions and their integration with grasping. Experiments show 76.39% success on hundreds of seen objects with grippers, and 57.91% on unseen peers, outperforming the strongest pose-reaching baseline by 20.52 and 17.79 percentage points, respectively. We also analyze emergent behaviors, including nonprehensile and prehensile repositioning, grasp acquisition that requires grasping after tipping, and table-assisted reorientation while grasping, and transfer to the real-world scenario. Project page available at lgswdn.github.io/Uni-PNP.

HMI Lab.title: Router Drift Control: Mitigating Off-Policy Degradation in Mixture-of-Experts Reinforcement Learning
HMI Lab.authors_text: Liangyao Jin, Zhixin Wang, Liming Liu, Mingjun Zhang, Zhengzhou Zhu
HMI Lab.summary: Router Drift Control (RDC) mitigates off-policy degradation in Mixture-of-Experts reinforcement learning by filtering high-drift responses, enhancing training accuracy and performance.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can become off-policy due to training-inference mismatch, mini-batch updates, and asynchronous training.The resulting mismatch is especially harmful in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where rollout--training discrepancies can change routing decisions and lead to router drift. Rollout Routing Replay (R3) mitigates this mismatch by reusing expert selections from the rollout stage during training. Our analysis shows that routing replay introduces gradient bias by losing contributions from experts selected by the training router but not the rollout router. To address this, we propose Router Drift Control (RDC), which uses routing disagreement between rollout and training as a signal of off-policy staleness and selectively rejects high-drift responses. The sequence-level filtering avoids gradient bias introduced by replay while preserving native expert selection and the associated learning signals for retained responses. Experiments show that RDC achieves larger gains as policy staleness increases and remains effective in asynchronous RL. In asynchronous training, RDC combined with Truncated Importance Sampling (TIS) improves the average peak validation accuracy across AIME 2024 and AIME 2025 by 5.5 points over TIS and 4.5 points over R3.

HMI Lab.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
HMI Lab.authors_text: Tianyi Guan, Yiding Wang, Haotong Yang, Siyuan Cao, Shirui Liu
HMI Lab.summary: ContinualSkillBench evaluates large language models' ability to evolve skills, revealing that while sequential execution enhances performance, skill retention and reuse vary significantly across models and tasks.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Modern agent frameworks equip large language models with external skill libraries to solve complex tasks. However, it remains unclear whether these systems can effectively evolve their skills and whether the resulting skills improve task-solving capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce ContinualSkillBench, a dynamic evaluation framework for in-context continual skill learning. It covers five domains, each with 100 tasks ordered by difficulty and opportunities for skill transfer. Our experiments show that sequential execution generally improves performance, but the gains vary substantially across models and domains. Moreover, across two models and three domains, retaining context and feedback without skill maintenance yields nearly the same mean performance as maintaining an explicit skill library. Explicit skills nevertheless provide selective benefits for tasks requiring reusable procedures or precise outputs. We further find that the weaker model (GPT-4o) accumulates more skills but reuses them less often, suggesting difficulty consolidating task-specific experience into reusable procedures. These findings show that current in-context skill evolution mechanisms can support continual adaptation, but still struggle to consistently consolidate experience into robust and transferable skills.

HMI Lab.title: From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents
HMI Lab.authors_text: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu
HMI Lab.summary: This survey presents a unified framework for execution provenance and evidence tracing in LLM agents, highlighting gaps in current research and proposing future directions.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are moving beyond text generation to planning, tool use, retrieval, memory access, environmental interaction, and multi-agent collaboration. Because their outputs depend on information and execution steps across an agent run, their execution processes are difficult to verify, debug, and audit. Even a correct final answer does not reveal which evidence supported its claims, whether tool calls were justified, how memory shaped decisions, or where execution failures originated. Relevant research addresses these questions across evidence attribution, tool-use safety, agent memory, and observability, but these areas emphasize different parts of the execution process. This survey brings them into a common framework through execution provenance, a typed graph of an agent run, and evidence tracing, its projection onto evidence-support relations, distinguishing evidence that supports a conclusion from execution that influences it. We introduce a six-dimensional taxonomy covering trace sources, evidence and execution units, provenance relations, tracing granularity and timing, representation forms, and trust functions, complemented by operational definitions of nine provenance relations and two cross-cutting attributes, provenance origin and trace assurance. Applying this framework to the surveyed systems and benchmarks reveals three gaps: limited integration of fine-grained provenance with multiple trust functions, no benchmark in our catalog that evaluates the complete provenance chain, and little reporting of tamper-evident or attested traces. These findings motivate research on unified trace schemas, semantic provenance, memory and multi-agent lineage, provenance-aware safety and recovery, realistic benchmarks, trace assurance, and privacy-aware auditing. Resources are available at https://github.com/xiaoqi-7/Agent-Tracing-Survey.

HMI Lab.title: Harness-Bench: Evaluating Agent Harnesses across Models and Realistic Workflows
HMI Lab.authors_text: Yilun Yao, Xinyu Tan, Chao-Hsuan Liu, Yaoming Li, Zhengyang Wang
HMI Lab.summary: Harness-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates the impact of harness configurations on LLM agent performance across realistic workflows, revealing significant variations in execution outcomes.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed as executable systems that use tools, modify workspaces, and produce concrete artifacts. In such workflows, performance depends not only on the base model, but also on the harness: the system layer that manages context, tools, state, constraints, permissions, tracing, and recovery. However, existing benchmarks typically abstract away execution, compare complete agent systems, or hold the harness fixed, making execution-layer variation difficult to study. We introduce Harness-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating configuration-level harness effects in realistic agent workflows. Harness-Bench evaluates representative harness configurations across multiple model backends under shared task environments, budgets, and evaluation protocols, while preserving each harness's native execution behavior. The benchmark contains 106 sandboxed offline tasks constructed from practical agent-use patterns and manually reviewed for realism, solvability, oracle-checkability, and integrity. Each run records final artifacts, execution traces, usage statistics, and validator outputs, enabling analysis beyond final completion. Across 5,194 execution trajectories, we observe substantial variation in completion, process quality, efficiency, and failure behavior across model-harness pairings. These results suggest that agent capability should be reported at the model-harness configuration level rather than attributed to the base model alone. Our analysis further identifies recurring execution-alignment failures, where plausible reasoning becomes decoupled from tool feedback, workspace state, evidence, or verifiable output contracts. Harness-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for diagnosing and improving reliable, efficient, and auditable agent execution stacks.

HMI Lab.title: CQDC-Warp: GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Quasi-Dynamic Simulation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
HMI Lab.authors_text: Yanchen Ding, Jiayi Chen, Jianfeng Xu, Wei Zhao, Li Yi
HMI Lab.summary: CQDC-Warp is a GPU-accelerated differentiable simulator that enhances contact-rich manipulation trajectory optimization, achieving high success rates and significantly faster trajectory generation times.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Efficient synthesis of contact-rich manipulation trajectories is essential for downstream robot learning. Gradient-based planning offers a promising approach, but jointly optimizing motion and contact decisions remains challenging. Meanwhile, many existing planners run on CPUs with limited throughput. We present CQDC-Warp, a GPU-accelerated differentiable quasi-dynamic simulator for batched model predictive control (MPC). We use it to study contact-guided trajectory optimization, in which intended robot--object contacts are specified before planning and encouraged through soft costs, while the simulated dynamics determine contact geometry and frictional response without a prescribed contact-mode schedule. Across $17{,}408$ trials on the $17$-object Allegro in-hand rotation benchmark, our framework achieves $79.8\%$ success, compared with $73.7\%$ for CFree and $65.2\%$ for IMPACT, and reduces mean trajectory-generation time by factors of $27.0$ and $50.2$, respectively. On a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 with $2{,}048$ parallel worlds, forward and backward throughput reach $2.06\times10^5$ and $2.25\times10^5$ world-steps per second, respectively. Further experiments cover manipulation with LEAP and Shadow hands, environmental contact exploitation, bimanual manipulation, whole-body control, and real-world trajectory replay on a Sharpa hand.

HMI Lab.title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent
HMI Lab.authors_text: Xuanyi Liu, Ruiqi Li, Siwei Ma
HMI Lab.summary: Mallea is a coding agent system that builds, steers, and memorizes dynamic worlds from text by coordinating object representations, behaviors, and visual memory.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Code world models represent world dynamics through explicit state and executable rules. We investigate how to coordinate object representations, behavioral revisions, and visual memory within this formulation. We present Mallea, a system for building, steering, and memorizing worlds from text. A coding agent infers object interaction requirements from the prompt and jointly plans object structure, properties, and rules, favoring compact representations that support those requirements. The world evolves under the planned rules; optional user actions steer it, while text requests can edit properties or extend capabilities with unaffected state preserved. Object texture memory retains reusable appearance only for whitebox-defined objects and adapts it as those objects change. The program advances world state, while a generative renderer combines current structure with remembered appearance. By organizing construction, intervention, and memory around the same objects, Mallea conditions subsequent observations on the latest state and compatible appearance. Project page: https://lxycopper.github.io/Mallea.

HMI Lab.title: Rubric Judgments Lack Uncertainty: Conformal Weighting for LLM Evaluation
HMI Lab.authors_text: Licheng Pan, Haocheng Yang, Haoxuan Li, Yuzhou Chen, Yichen Sun
HMI Lab.summary: The paper introduces Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), enhancing LLM evaluation by addressing judgment uncertainty in rubric-based assessments to improve reinforcement learning outcomes.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Rubric-based evaluation is widely used to assess large language model (LLM) outputs by decomposing quality into multiple criteria and assigning each a binary judgment from an LLM verifier. However, judgment certainty varies substantially across criteria. Existing methods uniformly aggregate these judgments into a final score, implicitly treating every criterion as equally certain and overlooking this heterogeneity. As a result, uncertain judgments remain incorporated into reward estimation without distinction, potentially yielding misleading training signals for downstream reinforcement learning (RL). To address this limitation, we propose Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), a training-free framework that quantifies criterion-level judgment uncertainty via conformal calibration. Specifically, URW elicits a soft uncertainty signal from a fixed pool of paraphrased judgment templates and converts it into a per-criterion weight using split-conformal $p$-values with provable coverage guarantees. Extensive experiments demonstrate that URW consistently improves pairwise preference accuracy and delivers stronger downstream RL alignment.

HMI Lab.title: ReasonUni: Reasoning-Augmented Reconstruction Advances Unified Multimodal Models
HMI Lab.authors_text: Feize Wu, Zhiyuan Yan, Yuhuan Hong, Yuwei Niu, Zongjian Li
HMI Lab.summary: ReasonUni enhances unified multimodal models by integrating reasoning into reconstructive post-training, improving image-to-text understanding and text-to-image generation through a novel reinforcement learning approach.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. We propose ReasonUni, a reasoning-augmented reconstructive post-training framework that extends this coupling beyond perception. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. To jointly optimize both modules, we introduce TreeGRPO, a tree-structured reinforcement learning method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path, then aggregates visual rewards to update both modules under a unified objective. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains in both understanding and generation, showing that reasoning-augmented reconstruction yields genuine mutual gains for UMMs.

HMI Lab.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
HMI Lab.authors_text: Ningxin Pan, Hanyu Li, Yeqing Shen, Ning Ding, Yehui Tang
HMI Lab.summary: The paper introduces RealtimeBench for evaluating LLM agents in dynamic environments and proposes TORSI to enhance their performance through structured learning across timescales.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. Two rounds raise Jev's average test score from 13.51 to 24.19 on a 0--100 progress scale, improving all six game types. The instructions also improve average scores for three other models without retuning. These findings point toward real-time intelligence: enabling powerful LLM agents to remain effective in a continuously changing world by organizing deliberation, learning, and action across timescales.

HMI Lab.title: RAP-WAM: Learning World-Action Models through Predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations
HMI Lab.authors_text: Yuanpeng He, Ceyao Zhang, Fangjing Li, Kefei Zhu, Lijian Li
HMI Lab.summary: RAP-WAM enhances policy learning in robotics by integrating predictive rehearsal and action perturbations, achieving significant performance improvements across various tasks without requiring separate scoring networks.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Recent world action models draw on video generation priors to jointly predict future observations and robot actions. Adapting these priors to control requires determining how future predictions should guide policy learning. RAP-WAM combines predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations (RAP) with future-supervised queries and Coupled Action Projection for policy learning. Predictive rehearsal trains on model-generated inputs while retaining recorded targets, and accumulates recurring errors into a spatial prior. We perturb actions and measure changes in video predictions. Action-response-based spatiotemporal credit assignment combines these responses, prediction error, and the rehearsal prior to allocate visual supervision; spatially aggregating the responses determines supervision intensity across future action steps. No separate scoring network or deployment-time probe is required. The base learns from a video-pretrained backbone without intermediate pretraining on external embodied data. We evaluate the fixed base and its agent-refined, task-conditioned system. On 42 RoboDojo tasks, their average success rates are 12.85% and 15.62%, with Scores of 17.86 and 20.59. Across 15 real-robot tasks, the complete system achieves 89.00% task-macro-average success, exceeding the strongest of five baselines by 37.67 percentage points. Across 315 fixed-output simulation windows, 45.21% of response-top20 positions fall outside error-top20, revealing information beyond prediction error. Videos and further details are available on the project website: https://rapwam.github.io/.

HMI Lab.title: Revisiting Embodied Chain-of-Thought for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
HMI Lab.authors_text: Nan Sun, Yuan Zhang, Yongkun Yang, Wentao Zhao, Peiyan Li
HMI Lab.summary: This paper introduces ERVLA, a vision-language-action model that enhances robotic manipulation through effective embodied chain-of-thought integration, achieving state-of-the-art performance in diverse tasks.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Embodied chain-of-thought (CoT) aims to bridge linguistic reasoning with robotic control, yet its effective form and integration remain underexplored. In this paper, we revisit embodied CoT for robotic control at an unprecedented scale. We curate the largest embodied CoT corpus to date, comprising 978,743 trajectories, 226.3M samples, and 2592.5 hours of data. Through extensive experiments, we show that effective CoT must ground high-level semantic understaning in concrete linguistic action guidance -- such as end-effector movement and image-space trajectories -- whereas high-level reasoning alone yields marginal gains. More importantly, we identify that explicit CoT does not scale reliably as an autoregressive action prefix, suffering from compounding errors during inference. To address these challenges, we propose ERVLA, a vision-language-action (VLA) model that effectively leverages linguistic reasoning in generalizable robot manipulation. ERVLA is trained using a CoT-dropout strategy, allowing the model to leverage rich reasoning traces during training while predicting actions directly without CoT during inference to bypass autoregressive instability. This approach enables reliable scaling with increasing pre-training data. ERVLA achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO-Plus with an 86.9\% success rate and reaches 53.2\% on VLABench, showcasing superior performance in out-of-distribution settings. Furthermore, ERVLA outperforms competitive state-of-the-art baselines in real-robot experiments, especially in handling semantic ambiguity and long-horizon tasks. Code, data, and model checkpoints are available on the project website: https://taoshuaiz.github.io/ERVLA/.

HMI Lab.title: Adapting the Interface, Not the Model: Runtime Harness Adaptation for Deterministic LLM Agents
HMI Lab.authors_text: Tianshi Xu, Huifeng Wen, Meng Li
HMI Lab.summary: The paper presents Life-Harness, a runtime adaptation method for LLM agents that enhances performance by addressing interface mismatches without altering model weights.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: LLM agents are shaped not only by their language models, but also by the runtime harness that mediates observation, tool use, action execution, feedback interpretation, and trajectory control. While existing agent adaptation methods mainly update model parameters, many failures in deterministic, rule-governed domains stem from mismatches at the model--environment interface. We propose Life-Harness, a lifecycle-aware runtime harness that improves frozen LLM agents without changing model weights or evaluation environments. Life-Harness evolves from training trajectories by converting recurring interaction failures into reusable interventions across environment contracts, procedural skills, action realization, and trajectory regulation, and remains fixed for evaluation on unseen tasks. We evaluate Life-Harness across eight environments from AgentBench, $τ$-bench, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld using 18 open-weight backbones, and further test three frontier models on seven environments. With Qwen3-4B-Instruct, Life-Harness exceeds Meta-Harness and AHE by 28.7 and 7.5 percentage points in mean accuracy across the seven shared environments, respectively, while using 8.5\% and 68.4\% fewer optimization tokens. The evolved harnesses also benefit GPT 5.5, Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, yielding an average accuracy gain of 3.5 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/Tianshi-Xu/Life-Harness.

HMI Lab.title: PhyMix: Towards Physically Consistent Single-Image 3D Indoor Scene Generation with Implicit--Explicit Optimization
HMI Lab.authors_text: Dongli Wu, Jingyu Hu, Ka-Hei Hui, Xiaobao Wei, Chengwen Luo
HMI Lab.summary: PhyMix enhances single-image 3D indoor scene generation by incorporating a Physics Evaluator and optimization strategies to ensure physical consistency while maintaining visual fidelity.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Existing methods for single-image 3D indoor scene generation often produce visually plausible results that violate real-world physical constraints, limiting their reliability in robotics, embodied AI, and virtual environment design. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Physics Evaluator that assesses four aspects (geometric priors, contact, stability, and deployability) through nine sub-constraints, establishing a benchmark for evaluating physical consistency. Our analysis reveals that even state-of-the-art methods produce scenes with substantial physical inconsistencies despite their visual plausibility. To address these limitations, we propose a framework that incorporates feedback from the Physics Evaluator into both training and inference to improve the physical plausibility of generated scenes. Specifically, PhyMix comprises two components: (i) implicit alignment via Scene-GRPO, a critic-free group-relative preference optimization strategy that uses physical evaluations to guide the generator toward physically plausible layouts, and (ii) explicit refinement via verifier-guided agentic repair, which translates evaluator diagnostics into executable scene-editing skills to correct residual violations at inference time. PhyMix unifies physical evaluation, preference-based alignment, and agentic inference-time correction to improve physical plausibility while retaining the observed scene content. Experiments show improvements in reconstruction quality and physical plausibility, while qualitative examples on stylized and real-world images illustrate the applicability of the framework beyond synthetic inputs.

HMI Lab.title: Stabilizing the Modality Gap: Null-Space Projected Continual Learning for Vision-Language Models
HMI Lab.authors_text: Tiantian Peng, Yuyang Liu, Shuo Yang, Qiuhe Hong, YongHong Tian
HMI Lab.summary: The paper presents FPCD, a framework that mitigates modality gap drift in continual learning for vision-language models by combining Fast Null-space Projection and Contrastive Distillation, achieving superior performance on benchmark tasks.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: The modality gap is intrinsic to multimodal alignment, where embeddings from different modalities remain partially separated in a shared representation space. In continual learning, CLIP-based vision-language models (VLMs) not only suffer catastrophic forgetting but also experience modality gap drift that disrupts the shared embedding geometry. Such drift degrades cross-modal alignment and generalization. We propose FPCD, an efficient framework combining Fast Null-space Projection (FNP) and Contrastive Distillation (CD). FNP accumulates compact Gram matrices of previous tasks' activations and projects gradients onto layer-adaptive approximate null spaces to reduce interference with learned representations. By replacing singular value decomposition with symmetric eigendecomposition, FNP accelerates projection-basis construction by a factor of 5-9. CD uses a small reference set to align the bidirectional image-to-text and text-to-image similarity distributions of the fine-tuned model with CLIP, thereby preserving pretrained cross-modal relations. On the 11-task MTIL benchmark, FPCD achieves 87.6% Last, 76.4% Average, and 65.2% Transfer. It also maintains more stable modality gaps and stronger zero-shot retrieval performance on COCO Captions and Flickr30k than competing methods. These results highlight the importance of controlling modality gap drift during continual adaptation of VLMs.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for enhanced goal-directed generation across various domains.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Blame Errant Words, Not the Canvas: Defect-Aware Spatial Credit Assignment for Visual Text Generation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Sujie Hu, Huaisong Zhang, Pujing Yang, Qian Wang, Xiaomin Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents TextDART and SCANNER, innovative models for defect-aware spatial credit assignment in visual text generation, enhancing accuracy and glyph quality through localized feedback.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. We identify two coupled limitations: recognition-based rewards often overlook visible glyph defects, while whole-image scalar feedback obscures the uneven quality of individual text regions. These limitations motivate our central principle: $\textit{Blame errant words, not the canvas}$, to effectively preserve local quality distinctions. First, we introduce $\mathbf{TextDART}$, a defect-aware region-targeted reward model that localizes individual text regions and independently evaluates their semantic correctness and glyph quality, providing fine-grained, region-precise feedback. Building on TextDART, we propose $\mathbf{SCANNER}$, which turns these regional judgments into spatially differentiated policy feedback. It normalizes rewards for each text target across sampled images and casts the resulting regional advantages onto the corresponding latent tokens. Extensive experiments on existing benchmarks and our newly established $\textbf{PolyText-Bench}$ demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in text accuracy and glyph fidelity. Project page: https://sujiehu.github.io/textdart-scanner

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiaye Lin, Ontai Tang, Jingtian Hao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MMSearch-OPD enhances long-horizon multimodal search agents through controllable data refinement, joint reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation, improving training and search capabilities.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhuoming Liu, Jinhong Lin, Lin Zhang, Yiwu Zhong, Yin Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The MaLoW framework internalizes historical context as lightweight parameter updates in streaming vision-language models, enhancing performance while minimizing latency and generalizing to action tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: When Reasoning Is Not Enough: Proactive Inquiry for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wei Cai, Jian Zhao, Yuchen Yuan, Xuelong Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces SAFE-PRO, a proactive inquiry framework enhancing safety in multimodal large language models by addressing intent-level risks and optimizing safety through clarifying questions.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can act unsafely when individually benign images and texts are interpreted jointly. Beyond implicit reasoning risk, where reasoning drifts toward harm, we identify intent-level risk, where cross-modal ambiguity silently commits the model to a hazardous premise that path-level optimization alone cannot correct. We propose SAFE-PRO, which uses a Risk-Conditioned Uncertainty (RCU) signal, combining predictive entropy with a learned cross-modal risk score, to decide when to ask safety-grounded clarifying questions and where to apply path optimization, under a reward that prioritizes safety and penalizes over-refusal. We also build SSUI-Dialog, a multimodal multi-turn dataset with dual-intent supervision, and theoretically analyze gradient variance and unsafe-completion risk under RCU. Across seven benchmarks and two base MLLMs, SAFE-PRO consistently improves safety over SRPO, roughly halves its over-refusal, and surpasses GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet in average single-turn safety.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: What Should Robot Policies Learn to Predict? Rethinking Supervision Targets in Vision-Language-Action Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haitao Shen, Hanyu Liu, Yihan Lin, Huiping Liu, Junbo Cui
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper proposes a unified framework for vision-language-action learning that optimally allocates training samples between action prediction and auxiliary objectives, enhancing policy performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are typically trained with action prediction as the primary supervision signal, since robots ultimately execute actions. Auxiliary objectives such as latent-action (LA) and future-vision (FV) prediction are often added to improve policy learning, yet they compete with action prediction for the same training budget. We ask whether, under a fixed budget, allocating a substantial share of training samples to such objectives, rather than to further action prediction, can improve policy learning. We build a unified VLA framework that couples a two-stream multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) with a sample-level router, which assigns each training sample to either action prediction or an auxiliary objective and thus makes supervision allocation explicit. Within this framework, we instantiate three LA targets based on LAPA and its DINO-feature variants, and three FV targets based on DINOv3, V-JEPA 2, and Wan2.2 representations. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, and four real-robot tasks, suitable LA and FV supervision outperforms action-only training under the same budget, even when action prediction receives no more than half of the training samples. FV generally outperforms LA, although the strongest LA target remains competitive on CALVIN. Diagnostic analyses suggest that DINO-based LA targets emphasize relative motion, whereas FV targets emphasize absolute position and task identity. We therefore argue that what robot policies learn to predict, and how training is allocated among these targets, should be treated as explicit design choices rather than defaulting to action-dominant training.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Uni-PNP: Unified Prehensile and Non-prehensile Policy Learning for Generalizable Object Pose Reaching
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wenxuan Zhu, Yuze Wang, Jiangran Lyu, Jiayi Chen, Yixin Zheng
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Uni-PNP introduces a unified policy for simultaneous prehensile and non-prehensile object manipulation, achieving superior performance in diverse scenarios compared to existing methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Object manipulation often requires combining non-prehensile actions with grasping. However, existing approaches typically develop these capabilities separately and integrate them by sequencing distinct primitives through prescribed intermediate objectives, limiting the coordination of contact motions and grasping. Their integration also remains sensitive to object and gripper geometry and depends on particular environmental supports, complicating real-world deployment. We present Uni-PNP, a unified policy that jointly learns prehensile and non-prehensile manipulation for object pose reaching across diverse objects and grippers. To achieve this, we first pretrain a geometry encoder to predict contact-induced object motion using a contact-dynamics dataset constructed from simulated interactions between diverse objects and grippers. We then train the policy in a two-stage reinforcement learning curriculum from graspable objects to ungraspable peers, encouraging the discovery of non-prehensile interactions and their integration with grasping. Experiments show 76.39% success on hundreds of seen objects with grippers, and 57.91% on unseen peers, outperforming the strongest pose-reaching baseline by 20.52 and 17.79 percentage points, respectively. We also analyze emergent behaviors, including nonprehensile and prehensile repositioning, grasp acquisition that requires grasping after tipping, and table-assisted reorientation while grasping, and transfer to the real-world scenario. Project page available at lgswdn.github.io/Uni-PNP.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Router Drift Control: Mitigating Off-Policy Degradation in Mixture-of-Experts Reinforcement Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Liangyao Jin, Zhixin Wang, Liming Liu, Mingjun Zhang, Zhengzhou Zhu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Router Drift Control (RDC) mitigates off-policy degradation in Mixture-of-Experts reinforcement learning by filtering high-drift responses, enhancing training accuracy and performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can become off-policy due to training-inference mismatch, mini-batch updates, and asynchronous training.The resulting mismatch is especially harmful in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where rollout--training discrepancies can change routing decisions and lead to router drift. Rollout Routing Replay (R3) mitigates this mismatch by reusing expert selections from the rollout stage during training. Our analysis shows that routing replay introduces gradient bias by losing contributions from experts selected by the training router but not the rollout router. To address this, we propose Router Drift Control (RDC), which uses routing disagreement between rollout and training as a signal of off-policy staleness and selectively rejects high-drift responses. The sequence-level filtering avoids gradient bias introduced by replay while preserving native expert selection and the associated learning signals for retained responses. Experiments show that RDC achieves larger gains as policy staleness increases and remains effective in asynchronous RL. In asynchronous training, RDC combined with Truncated Importance Sampling (TIS) improves the average peak validation accuracy across AIME 2024 and AIME 2025 by 5.5 points over TIS and 4.5 points over R3.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Tianyi Guan, Yiding Wang, Haotong Yang, Siyuan Cao, Shirui Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: ContinualSkillBench evaluates large language models' ability to evolve skills, revealing that while sequential execution enhances performance, skill retention and reuse vary significantly across models and tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Modern agent frameworks equip large language models with external skill libraries to solve complex tasks. However, it remains unclear whether these systems can effectively evolve their skills and whether the resulting skills improve task-solving capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce ContinualSkillBench, a dynamic evaluation framework for in-context continual skill learning. It covers five domains, each with 100 tasks ordered by difficulty and opportunities for skill transfer. Our experiments show that sequential execution generally improves performance, but the gains vary substantially across models and domains. Moreover, across two models and three domains, retaining context and feedback without skill maintenance yields nearly the same mean performance as maintaining an explicit skill library. Explicit skills nevertheless provide selective benefits for tasks requiring reusable procedures or precise outputs. We further find that the weaker model (GPT-4o) accumulates more skills but reuses them less often, suggesting difficulty consolidating task-specific experience into reusable procedures. These findings show that current in-context skill evolution mechanisms can support continual adaptation, but still struggle to consistently consolidate experience into robust and transferable skills.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This survey presents a unified framework for execution provenance and evidence tracing in LLM agents, highlighting gaps in current research and proposing future directions.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are moving beyond text generation to planning, tool use, retrieval, memory access, environmental interaction, and multi-agent collaboration. Because their outputs depend on information and execution steps across an agent run, their execution processes are difficult to verify, debug, and audit. Even a correct final answer does not reveal which evidence supported its claims, whether tool calls were justified, how memory shaped decisions, or where execution failures originated. Relevant research addresses these questions across evidence attribution, tool-use safety, agent memory, and observability, but these areas emphasize different parts of the execution process. This survey brings them into a common framework through execution provenance, a typed graph of an agent run, and evidence tracing, its projection onto evidence-support relations, distinguishing evidence that supports a conclusion from execution that influences it. We introduce a six-dimensional taxonomy covering trace sources, evidence and execution units, provenance relations, tracing granularity and timing, representation forms, and trust functions, complemented by operational definitions of nine provenance relations and two cross-cutting attributes, provenance origin and trace assurance. Applying this framework to the surveyed systems and benchmarks reveals three gaps: limited integration of fine-grained provenance with multiple trust functions, no benchmark in our catalog that evaluates the complete provenance chain, and little reporting of tamper-evident or attested traces. These findings motivate research on unified trace schemas, semantic provenance, memory and multi-agent lineage, provenance-aware safety and recovery, realistic benchmarks, trace assurance, and privacy-aware auditing. Resources are available at https://github.com/xiaoqi-7/Agent-Tracing-Survey.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Harness-Bench: Evaluating Agent Harnesses across Models and Realistic Workflows
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yilun Yao, Xinyu Tan, Chao-Hsuan Liu, Yaoming Li, Zhengyang Wang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Harness-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates the impact of harness configurations on LLM agent performance across realistic workflows, revealing significant variations in execution outcomes.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed as executable systems that use tools, modify workspaces, and produce concrete artifacts. In such workflows, performance depends not only on the base model, but also on the harness: the system layer that manages context, tools, state, constraints, permissions, tracing, and recovery. However, existing benchmarks typically abstract away execution, compare complete agent systems, or hold the harness fixed, making execution-layer variation difficult to study. We introduce Harness-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating configuration-level harness effects in realistic agent workflows. Harness-Bench evaluates representative harness configurations across multiple model backends under shared task environments, budgets, and evaluation protocols, while preserving each harness's native execution behavior. The benchmark contains 106 sandboxed offline tasks constructed from practical agent-use patterns and manually reviewed for realism, solvability, oracle-checkability, and integrity. Each run records final artifacts, execution traces, usage statistics, and validator outputs, enabling analysis beyond final completion. Across 5,194 execution trajectories, we observe substantial variation in completion, process quality, efficiency, and failure behavior across model-harness pairings. These results suggest that agent capability should be reported at the model-harness configuration level rather than attributed to the base model alone. Our analysis further identifies recurring execution-alignment failures, where plausible reasoning becomes decoupled from tool feedback, workspace state, evidence, or verifiable output contracts. Harness-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for diagnosing and improving reliable, efficient, and auditable agent execution stacks.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: CQDC-Warp: GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Quasi-Dynamic Simulation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yanchen Ding, Jiayi Chen, Jianfeng Xu, Wei Zhao, Li Yi
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: CQDC-Warp is a GPU-accelerated differentiable simulator that enhances contact-rich manipulation trajectory optimization, achieving high success rates and significantly faster trajectory generation times.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Efficient synthesis of contact-rich manipulation trajectories is essential for downstream robot learning. Gradient-based planning offers a promising approach, but jointly optimizing motion and contact decisions remains challenging. Meanwhile, many existing planners run on CPUs with limited throughput. We present CQDC-Warp, a GPU-accelerated differentiable quasi-dynamic simulator for batched model predictive control (MPC). We use it to study contact-guided trajectory optimization, in which intended robot--object contacts are specified before planning and encouraged through soft costs, while the simulated dynamics determine contact geometry and frictional response without a prescribed contact-mode schedule. Across $17{,}408$ trials on the $17$-object Allegro in-hand rotation benchmark, our framework achieves $79.8\%$ success, compared with $73.7\%$ for CFree and $65.2\%$ for IMPACT, and reduces mean trajectory-generation time by factors of $27.0$ and $50.2$, respectively. On a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 with $2{,}048$ parallel worlds, forward and backward throughput reach $2.06\times10^5$ and $2.25\times10^5$ world-steps per second, respectively. Further experiments cover manipulation with LEAP and Shadow hands, environmental contact exploitation, bimanual manipulation, whole-body control, and real-world trajectory replay on a Sharpa hand.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xuanyi Liu, Ruiqi Li, Siwei Ma
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Mallea is a coding agent system that builds, steers, and memorizes dynamic worlds from text by coordinating object representations, behaviors, and visual memory.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Code world models represent world dynamics through explicit state and executable rules. We investigate how to coordinate object representations, behavioral revisions, and visual memory within this formulation. We present Mallea, a system for building, steering, and memorizing worlds from text. A coding agent infers object interaction requirements from the prompt and jointly plans object structure, properties, and rules, favoring compact representations that support those requirements. The world evolves under the planned rules; optional user actions steer it, while text requests can edit properties or extend capabilities with unaffected state preserved. Object texture memory retains reusable appearance only for whitebox-defined objects and adapts it as those objects change. The program advances world state, while a generative renderer combines current structure with remembered appearance. By organizing construction, intervention, and memory around the same objects, Mallea conditions subsequent observations on the latest state and compatible appearance. Project page: https://lxycopper.github.io/Mallea.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Rubric Judgments Lack Uncertainty: Conformal Weighting for LLM Evaluation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Licheng Pan, Haocheng Yang, Haoxuan Li, Yuzhou Chen, Yichen Sun
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), enhancing LLM evaluation by addressing judgment uncertainty in rubric-based assessments to improve reinforcement learning outcomes.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Rubric-based evaluation is widely used to assess large language model (LLM) outputs by decomposing quality into multiple criteria and assigning each a binary judgment from an LLM verifier. However, judgment certainty varies substantially across criteria. Existing methods uniformly aggregate these judgments into a final score, implicitly treating every criterion as equally certain and overlooking this heterogeneity. As a result, uncertain judgments remain incorporated into reward estimation without distinction, potentially yielding misleading training signals for downstream reinforcement learning (RL). To address this limitation, we propose Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), a training-free framework that quantifies criterion-level judgment uncertainty via conformal calibration.
